thread.title: Morning Movers: Caterpillar Gives the Dow Wings

author: Teresa Rivas
title: Morning Movers: Caterpillar Gives the Dow Wings
text:
By Teresa Rivas July 30, 2018 9:24 a.m. ET Monday Motivation. The Dow Jones Industrial Average is trading higher this morning, helped by Caterpillar (CAT) earnings. In today's Morning Movers , we...
Illustration: Getty Images •...review the myriad earnings results due out this week;
•...debate if markets can make headway without tech;
•....and note a selloff in Tyson Foods (TSN) after its updated guidance.
The Tech Question
Markets appear poised to start the week on an upbeat note, with all three major indexes edging up in early trading.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average is leading the way, up 0.2%, boosted by earnings from industrial giant Caterpillar (CAT)–more on that below–while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite are both up less than 0.1% at recent check.
There's no shortage of news this week to push stocks: Not only is it another hectic week of earnings, including tech giant Apple (AAPL,) as the second-quarter reporting season is in full swing, but the latest Federal Reserve meeting will conclude on Wednesday, and Friday we'll get July nonfarm payroll data to parse.
Of course, Faang stocks, which, along with Apple, include Facebook (FB), Amazon.com (AMZN), Netflix (NFLX), and Alphabet (GOOGL), haven't had a great track record this quarter, with Facebook and Netflix falling after earnings , and Amazon ending only slightly higher after reporting a strong quarter .
While the market is more than just tech stocks , that sector has certainly been the driver of its gains for more than a year. So what happens if it starts to fizzle? With the S&P 500 back within striking distance of its old highs, will earnings from other firms and macro data allow it to notch new records, or will Apple–which has been grappling with lackluster iPhone sales –deal it another blow?
Datatrek's Nicholas Colas writes that even if tech declines 10% between now and the end of the year, that will still give it a 1.1% 2018 gain, and it's possible for the S&P 500 to continue to advance, even though the sector accounts for more than a quarter of its weighting.
It can do so if other large sectors can do well. Colas believes that investors will be willing to jump ship to health care if tech starts to falter, although with its Faang weighting, consumer discretionary might be less able to shake off tech blues. That leaves financials and industrials as the "make-or-break" sectors. "The former needs the yield curve to steepen (something we think likely). The latter could really use some good news on the trade front (possible, if only because the president likely wants some wins to campaign with ahead of midterm elections)," Colas explains.
Of course, even with the spate of data due out this week, trade tensions are never far from mind. While the U.S. and European Union have tentatively agreed to work things out, there's nothing on paper yet. Yet bulls are nonetheless still happy that a meeting between the two powers resulted in such a positive outcome, especially given pessimism going in (much the opposite occurred Friday, when the White House talked up GDP numbers only to have those high hopes dashed, even with a still-strong second-quarter showing).
With the U.S. and Europe potentially allied again, is China on the ropes? It's reportedly refocusing fiscal policy to try to counter trade tensions, and a number of analysts think that the recent bounce in Chinese stocks may not last. "It is in President Trump’s best interest to try to minimize any negative impact of the trade tariffs going into the midterm elections that are now only a little over three months away," writes Tigress Financial's Ivan Feinseth .
Still, he too notes that with "key macroeconomic themes remain in place, including fiscal policy tailwinds and strong consumer sentiment and record low unemployment" earnings can remain the driver of July gains, as we approach the busiest reporting week of the season: Along with Apple, more than 700 companies will report, including 174 S&P components.
We'll be glued to our iPhones to bring you the latest.
Morning Movers
Earnings & News
Illustration: Agence France-Presse/Getty Images Caterpillar (CAT) is up 3.4% to $147.37 after reporting second-quarter earnings . The industrial equipment maker earned $2.97 a share on revenue of $14.01 billion. Analysts were looking for earnings of $2.74 on revenue of $14.09 billion. For the full year, it expects EPS of $11 to $12, compared with the $10.75 consensus estimate.
First Data (FDC) is up 6.9% to $24.18 after reporting second-quarter earnings . The retail tech firm earned 39 cents a share on revenue of $2.23 billion. Analysts were looking for earnings of 37 cents on revenue of $2.2 billion.
Seagate Technology (STX) is up 1.5% to $55.50 after reporting fourth-quarter earnings . The hard-drive maker earned $1.62 a share on revenue of $2.84 billion. Analysts were looking for earnings of $1.45 on revenue of $2.8 billion. It also announced its CFO is stepping down.
Tyson Foods (TSN) is down 4.8% to $60.55 after reporting adjusting its full-year outlook . The meat processor now expects EPS of $5.70 to $6, down from $6.55 to $6.70 previously.
Upgrades & Downgrades
Illustration: Kena Betancur/AFP/Getty Images AT&T (T) is up 1.2% to $31.45 after Bank of America Merrill Lynch upgraded it to Buy.
Avis Budget Group (CAR) is up 2.7% to $34.15 after Northcoast upgraded it to Buy.
Cabot Oil & Gas (COG) is up 0.5% to $22.92 after Susquehanna upgraded it to Positive.
Colgate Palmolive (CL) is down 0.7% to $66.19 after Macquarie downgraded it to Neutral.
Juniper Networks (JNPR) is up 2% to $26.72 after Deutsche Bank upgraded it to Buy.
